notes.title: The 4 year anniversary update!
notes.content:
[p]Hi everyone,[/p][p]
It’s (almost) the 4 year anniversary of Severed Steel’s launch so I thought I’d put together a small celebration![/p][p]
[b]First off, I’ve launched an update that fixes up and polishes a variety of things.[/b] Full patch notes below but highlights include:[/p][list][*][p]Faster daily challenge generation[/p][/*][*][p]Improvements to how the arm cannon works[/p][/*][*][p]Improved gib physics[/p][/*][*][p]Significant tweaks to Rogue Steel’s rules and unlocks[/p][/*][/list][p]
[b]I’ve also put together a making-of documentary on Severed Steel[/b], check it out if you are interested in game design or how games are made![/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="a86JrLRYjR0;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
[/p][p][b]Finally, I’ve uploaded 4 development builds of Severed Steel so you can experience what the game was like in different stages of its development.[/b] You can try out things like the oldest build I could find, a prototype bank heist campaign mission, and a glue gun mode for the arm cannon. Be sure to read the readme![/p][p][url="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LhX2gq-fRV4XcQiFJwgia8lvlQnA0a2P/view?usp=sharing"]Google Drive download[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for reading and I hope you enjoy![/p][p]
[/p][p]-Matt[/p][p]
[/p][p]FULL PATCH NOTES:[/p][p]
[/p][p]Balance:[/p][p]-Reduced time needed to fully charge cannon[/p][p]-Buffed damage of charged cannon shots (full cannon will 1 shot heavies)[/p][p]-Charged cannon shots deal larger voxel damage radius[/p][p]-Reduced unlock requirements for rogue skins[/p][p]-All rogue cards have a chance to be drawn at any time during Rogue, instead of limiting some to mid and end run.[/p][p]-Less chance of same cards being drawn twice in a row in Rogue Steel[/p][p]-Cannon now doesn’t force shoot when charged to full capacity[/p][p]-Reduced explosive shield XP by 20%[/p][p]
[/p][p]Bug fixes:[/p][p]-Now use Steam servers for daily challenge time instead of third party ones, should improve update time and fix blocked regions not being able to play.[/p][p]-Fixed improper score tracking in Rogue steel, in-game score meter and post game score summary should now match.[/p][p]-Fixed cannon double shot after a fully charged shot[/p][p]-Fixed coin count clipping when greater than 2 digits[/p][p]-Fixed instances where resolution would be set to 85% scale[/p][p]-Enabled high dpi awareness which hopefully helps with missed clicks in borderless mode with desktop scaling[/p][p]
[/p][p]Performance / visuals:[/p][p]-Precompile shaders on first boot in DX12, should reduce stutters for new players. [/p][p]-Gib chunks now launch in direction depending on impact direction[/p][p]-Updated localizations for Japanese, Russian, Turkish, Chinese Traditional, Chinese Modern[/p][p]-More screen refresh rate options[/p][p]

[/p]

notes.title: THE STYLE UPDATE IS NOW LIVE
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

[b]Lots of new content just went live! [/b]

[previewyoutube=W5X3tPkwElc;full][/previewyoutube]

We have added a new style ranking system to Firefight mode which rewards you for being stylish! There's 30 types of stunts available to you to boost your score, read about them in the Firefight setup screen. Firefight mode should feel way more satisfying and way less grindy! Plus there's a bunch of new levels pre-unlocked for you to try out.

You can also now send living enemies flying through the air with your kicks, thrown weapons, and explosions. They'll get back up if you don't finish them off. This new system creates some extremely stylish combat moments! If you prefer the old way check game settings to turn it off.

There's also some great new music and lots of small quality of life tweaks requested on the discord and steam forums. Full notes below!

Please note that we are making all new leaderboards because of the new scoring system, if you want to access the old build and leaderboards they will be made available on a beta branch.

Thanks for reading and enjoy the new content,

-MattWLA

[h2]New Features:[/h2]

[h3]Firefight 2.0:[/h3] A complete overhaul with a strong emphasis on style! Achieve higher scores with stylish gameplay and check your rank at the end of each round. New leaderboards are available for all levels.

[h3]Live Ragdolls:[/h3] Enemies now have a chance to be knocked over without dying. Beware, they will get back up to continue the fight if not dealt with! (Note: Melee attacks and explosions trigger this state if they're not lethal. This feature can be toggled off in settings.)

[h3]Hit Markers:[/h3] Customize your experience with 5 different hit marker options. Disabling hit markers is also available for players who prefer it.

[h3]New Firefight Levels:[/h3] Dive into 8 fresh firefight levels, ready for action.

[h3]New Music for Firefight:[/h3] Groove to 7 new tracks in firefight mode, along with additional campaign tracks now in rotation.

[h3]Bug Fixes & Tweaks:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Bullet & Fire Interaction: Fixed issues preventing bullets and fire from passing through glass.
[*] Weapon Throwing: Weapons can now be thrown through glass.
[*] Mobility: Sliding and diving against doors will now open them.
[*] Explosives: Addressed odd behaviors with explosives interacting with grass.
[*] Physics: Adjusted gib physics for a more natural feel.
[*] Settings: New options to hide the flashing objective text and disable checkpoints.
[*] Quick Reset: Fixed a softlock issue occurring when using quick reset during the victory fade. (Note: Reset is currently disabled during this phase as a quick fix.)
[*] Cannon Shots: New setting to center cannon shots on the camera.
[*] Mission Select: Tutorial levels are now accessible.
[*] Visuals: Adjusted sky color and fixed issues with the bonus campaign completion screen.
[*] NPC Interaction: Ragdolls will now more reliably break glass.
[*] Daily Challenge: Ensured deterministic weapon spawns.
[*] Props: Removed shake from props for a smoother experience.
[*] Weapon Interaction: Heavy weapons and lasers will no longer be stopped by rockets.
[*] Sound FX: New sound effects for throwing weapons.
[*] Collision: Adjusted collision parameters for backpacks.
[*] Headshots: Shots near the head are now considered headshots.
[*] Controller Support: Restored the throw button functionality.
[*] Gameplay Tweaks: Adjusted "attack the weakpoint" for better melee interaction, and ensured shots on heavies work from any angle.
[*] Aim Assistance: Smoothed out the motion for kick auto-aim.
[*] Melee Attacks: Updated so they no longer cause headshots.
[*] Enemy Interaction: Hitting an enemy with a thrown weapon now disarms them.
[*] Level Editor: Fixed an issue where "Rogue Steel" mutators carried over.
[*] Leaderboards: Now accessible from the Firefight victory screen.
[*] Disco Lights: Added the ability for editors to spawn disco lights.
[*] Audio: Lowered the volume of the breath loop.
[*] Firefight Challenges: Made some challenges easier to complete.
[*] OC Cannon: Now classified as a cheat.
[*] Mutators: Enjoy 5 mutators in Friday's daily challenges.
[*] Seasonal Fun: Look out for jack-o-lanterns this October!
[*] Mutator Lineup: Removed 'lowgrav' and 'steelcraft' from the daily mutator lineup.

You can also customize your rogue run with features like perma-death if you want more (or less) challenge!

notes.title: 1 Year Anniversary
notes.content:
[h3]Hi everyone, thanks for stopping by to read this announcement - we have some big news![/h3]

Severed Steel launched on PC 1 year ago. To celebrate this anniversary I’d like to announce the next update which will let players experience Severed Steel in a whole new way.

[h3]COMING SOON: ROGUE STEEL.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/b213e42024ecb13024d6a29a94fac350db896623.png[/img]

Rogue Steel is a new way to play Severed Steel inspired by the Rogue-lite genre of games. Rogue Steel mode generates a short campaign (a “run”) by randomly shuffling together 10 levels from the base game and content expansions. After every level you draw 3 random perk cards from a deck, and choose one to keep. Each card you choose to keep alters the rules of the game to buff the player (e.g. dive twice as far, triple jump, double magazine size) or add challenge (buff enemy HP, turn floor to lava, disable slowmo).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/7a6b2cc081df38e0c170c6bedad69c25aba0051b.png[/img]

Cards can stack in interesting ways. For example: Combine a card that makes enemies heads bigger, with a card that gives you an extra bullet when you kill an enemy, with a card that gives all guns perfect accuracy… you can imagine the results!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/ebe89139f011b36c2ab6a4479d5f857f243c232b.png[/img]

Many of you are wondering, will there be perma-death? That will be an option for those who want the challenge!

When you complete a run you get all the cards you chose added to your collection. Collect all the cards to earn unlockables and achievements. Each run is also scored, with the cards that make runs harder buffing your score - get high scores to also unlock stuff! 

The Rogue Steel update launches Oct. 1st, and will also feature new levels and weapons! 

Thank you for reading this! I’m excited to launch Rogue Steel mode and I hope the community enjoys playing it as much as I do.

-Matt

P.S. If you’ve got an idea for a perk card please leave a comment!

notes.title: Campaign Update 3.0
notes.content:
[h2][b] Major Feature Additions[/b][/h2]

[h1]12 new levels[/h1]

     The highlight of this update. Many level editor features were made to support the experiences the levels wanted to create. The larger scale of the newer levels necessitated optimization of AI behavior, the benefits of which also carry over to the base levels.

[h1]New cannon mode, meta grenade[/h1]

     Given the level reorder and properties of the initial campaign, players ended up entering the final level ‘The Wall’, with a brand new arm cannon type, immediately after unlocking it. The beam flamethrower arm cannon mode was initially also used in the ‘Estate’ level. The sudden confusing and underwhelming nature of the overcharged cannon necessitated the introduction of an improved late-game upgrade. The Meta Grenade has similar uses to the Plasma Grenade, but has more charges, no drop-off, faster travel speed, and more enemy damage. Rather than giving the player something different and unfamiliar in the final levels, we wanted to improve the player’s current ability to express themselves by increasing the usability of the standard arm cannon.

[h1]Adds Specialist npc[/h1]

     A recolor of the standard enemy type, but with new guns, doubled movement speed and health, and crouches less often. The majority of enemy types in the game can be killed quickly, even without headshots. Making a tougher, faster, more aggressive enemy type fills a niche that the old enemy roster didn’t have. Their dropped weapons include a mix of new and underused guns, which mirror, but are an improvement upon, the standard enemy loadout.

[h1]Added suppressed deagle[/h1]

     The only previous sidearm type weapon that was suppressed was a fast, high capacity, burst fire pistol. A slower weapon with the same damage as the deagle provides a sidegrade option.

[h1]Added suppressed mac10[/h1]

     The smg class of weapons didn’t have a suppressed option, and a huge suppressor on a tiny gun looks cool.

[h1]Added sawn off shotgun[/h1]

     A requested weapon by bloody, the sawn off is dropped by specialists and heavies. High damage, low range, low capacity weapons are fun. It is capable of 1 shotting a heavy enemy if enough pellets hit.

[h1]Added lever action[/h1]

     Guns with manual actions are cool, a one armed protagonist who is also able to use such a gun is even cooler.

[h1]Tweaked music throughout campaign[/h1]

     Many tracks created by Floating Door for the OST were unused. Adding new levels interspaced in the campaign provided the opportunity to revise the existing bgm. 

[h1]New achievements[/h1]

[h2][b]Editor updates[/b][/h2]


[h1][b]Editor Trigger Volume updates[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*] Trigger volumes can make events happen

[/list]

[h1][b]Editor Prop updates[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*] Alphabetized id selection in editor

[*] Add invuln related prop actions
[*] New no cannon damage flag (props take hp dmg but no cannon visual dmg)
[*] Add show health bar action for props
[/list]

[h1][b]Editor Action updates[/b][/h1]

[list]
[*] Add unlimited cannon ammo action
[*] Added kill all npcs action
[*] Added disable AI action
[*] Added bgm related actions: DropPitch, RaisePitch, StopMusic, PlayMusic, PlayIcePrison, PlaySolarpunk
[*] Added lighting related actions: some ambient light events, KillLights, RestoreLights

[/list]

[list]
[*] Made rectangle selection more accurate

[*] Door and campaign markers snap on spawn
[*] Added more guns to editor spawns
[*] Enabled basic checkpoint setup
[/list]

[h1][b]Stunt Balancing[/b][/h1]

[list]
[*] Added 0.5 seconds to jump and double jump startup
[/list]
	Jumping from a flat surface gave a small amount of stunt, about 0.15 seconds, at the beginning and at the end of the jump arc. Both trigger because of the passive stunt status granted when being above 850 units of speed. The additional forced stunt time of 0.5 seconds allows the player to stay in stunt mode until near the apex of the jump. This allows a larger and more forgiving window to transfer from sliding or standing to wallrun, behaves more similarly to the stunt time granted from walljumping and doublejumping from a walljump, and overall allows for safer vertical movement.
[list]
[*] Kicking door gives 1.0 seconds stunt
[*] Leaving fan gives .5 seconds stunt
[*] Stunt timers now check that they won't interrupt an already longer running stunt timer before activating	
[/list]

[h1][b]Level Balancing[/b][/h1]

[h1][b]Weapon Balancing[/b][/h1]

     Many weapons felt underwhelming. Visual tweaks in randomized gun attachments and audio tweaks in gun sounds help distinguish them from each other. All smg type weapons, the most commonly used type in the game, received both a base ROF buff as well as a ROF buff while in bullet time. The DB12’s 2 shot burst fire was seldom useful, changing it into a full auto weapon fills a role not yet seen in the shotgun weapon type. The L86, as a weapon that is only placed in levels and not dropped by enemies, felt ineffective and boring, with rifle tier damage but horrible accuracy. Increasing its accuracy, ROF, and giving it the same ROF buff smgs have in bullet time makes it stand out as a powerful gun to use.

     Many of the new levels are larger and have higher enemy counts than previous levels, using enemy spawners was necessary to reduce CPU load, tweaking and optimizing spawner properties became necessary. Many older levels did not feature extremely long sightlines, so AI detection and behavior was adjusted to reduce excessive CPU use from AI pathfinding to distant players.

notes.title: COMMUNITY MAPS SPOTLIGHT
notes.content:
[i][b]Welcome to another community maps spotlight! This latest look at some of the user-made levels comes from 'bloody', who works on level designs for Severed Steel, and is a much deeper dive into the selected maps.[/b][/i]

Hello gamers,

While there has already been a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1227690/view/3133937847587097353]post highlighting community maps made recently[/url], I wanted to share my excitement and thoughts on some of my favorites that haven't already been covered.

[h3][b]THE BUMKER (created by 'ZURA')[/b][/h3]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2633287790&searchtext=
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/fb899c44214623c10d58d3225b7bcd466b78901a.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/99196568f360b811e2de0cb28d180cf34939b17c.jpg[/img]

This underground bunker map goes deceptively deep, the Z-axis being 640 units, the max value possible being 1024. For comparison, Portal Lab's bounds are 256x256x256, and Train's bounds are 1024 lengthwise. The path is long and while the first 2 corridors set expectations to be on a predictable and linear experience, it quickly becomes unpredictable with the enemy density and routing. Searching for the next pathway downwards becomes an adventure. 

During the latter half, the next rooms are sealed off with thick voxel walls without any alternative routes. The enemy composition of the room prior ensures there are plenty of backpacks left to charge the arm cannon. It adds to the sense of exploring a reinforced compound not meant to be traversed. Overall it reminds me of the bunker in Katana Zero. In the campaign map Armory, backpack enemies are sparse but plenty of grenade launchers are put near/around the exit to ensure the player is able to complete the level without using the arm cannon.

Things I'd recommned would be more consistency in the visual language and using lighting to convey depth. Blue electronic voxels are used to show which walls are meant to be destroyed via the arm cannon, but the placement is not as consistent as it could be to aid player direction, such as the blue outline on the floor of the rusty elevator shaft rather than around the doorframe, or the use of blue voxels around the fan grate meant to be destroyed, rather than specifically blue electric. Lighting on the map is also left flat. Setting global lighting to Dim and adding lighting manually, but slowly reducing the brightness as the level goes lower would add to the feeling of going deeper into the earth. I'd also maybe add a portal connecting the very end of the map to the very top in case players need to backtrack and reach missed enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/a91e4c816ca02143c67dda9bb7eb078b5d9d6902.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/217f9b5c63c378af61add355e2195684dcf582f9.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/eabfbe25c80f851e23c86317b7d958372ffaf270.jpg[/img]

Overall a great map. ZURA made something with the editor that stands out from the maps available in the base game. It features unique aspects of the game and of ZURA's creativity that would not work as well in other game's systems.

[h3][b]BALUSTRADE (created by 'Equinox')[/b][/h3]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2613898158&searchtext=
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/26e66dcc68135d2cbb75a2e18c2cc2a0a936818f.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/d355bd78e1d37cf6b3578edb3e3936295d1c38f4.jpg[/img]

An arena map with a simple symmetrical layout, what stood out to me were the aesthetics. Balustrade effectively uses orange electronic voxels to convey the angles of the corners, as well as the explorable area of the center column. Equinox seemed to have a grasp on the principles I followed when making maps such as Waste Management and Corridor. In Waste Management, I used blue electronic voxels to highlight horizontal edges the player can navigate on or around, and Corridor uses yellow electronic and green electronic to highlight filled and hollow pipe edges. The center column of Balustrade has the middle circular arena colored with maroon and bordered with red electronic. While it accentuates the roundness it also contrasts with the angular nature of the bordering walls. This also helps show players which section of wall they could destroy and enter through quickly with voxel destruction.

Thoughtful ideas are also present in the portal layout and orientantion as well as the location and size of the windows. Face the corner and walk through, you still face the corner but on a different vertical level. Face the center and go through, you still face the center. It would have been easy to copy and drag the portal above or below as needed, but this orientation allows easier readjustment after teleporting. Windows are placed and sized so that wallrunning into the corner room is uninterrupted, and the location of those rooms are easier to notice thanks to the previously mentioned use of the orange lines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/bf56921c6dd1c0438486bf7ebd90d426590972cc.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/cabb8d146796e7a144f7bb300b92389dbfc1e944.jpg[/img]

Due to the scale and layout there are not many instances where using the arm cannon to create paths through geometry is viable. Using the arm cannon on hanging walkways makes holes enemies can fall through and have to avoid, but the area below the bottommost level's center colum and outer walkways are solid all the way down which prevents such tactics. The middle of the center column is also thick, which prevents quickly going down through the floor or up through the ceiling. The layout also necessitates frequent wallrunning in/around the column or along the outer walls due to the openness, and due to the distance between wallrunning surfaces. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/ad4cd6a9ae21af8ac85b144181f345e757159b95.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/1df3c12b9d0a1f941fc9bd21b25459b2f7428ced.jpg[/img]

However, none of the things said in the previous paragraph detract from the enjoyabiliy of this map. I do not know Equinox, but I notice and respect things like how the walkways and center column are oriented perfectly to the grid. They seemed to have an idea they wanted to express within the engine of Severed Steel, and I think it is expressed beautifully.

[h3][b]TOWERS (created by 'Rick')[/b][/h3]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2630702779&searchtext=
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/73f745833b84b0e14087a7f80bb5773dd868cccb.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/59fb03e1cc59239c7488c451c25a2e18c7e39460.jpg[/img]

Rick's Towers 2 map was already covered in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1227690/view/3133937847587097353]previous community map spotlight post[/url]. I enjoy both, and wanted to compare and contrast the two. Both maps garner my respect in the geometry of each buliding. The ceilings of Towers have unique aspects and layouts to them, compared to the mostly uniform shape and sealed layout of Towers 2. The blue building's windows, while uniform in the placement of the frames, have subtle differences showing what floors can be jumped into. Use of fans and portals also allow players to ascend the tallest structures quickly.

Towers also makes use of cleverly placed explosives that reward players attentive to their envionrment. Unusual positioning of glowing voxels prompts inspection, and consistent visual language aids in the clarity of purpose. Noticing glowing red/yellow voxels in a building that's mostly blue and grey rewards the player with new routes or weapons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/5513c59d70b3ae5b6c3c218a270a0d5140358345.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/0a98ad4b7e7cf09556488a0d63fc71feafc3638d.jpg[/img]

While the layout of the buildings are interesting inside, interconnectivity between buildings is also used in interesting ways. Portals connecting different bulidings, pathways between different floors of adjacent structures, holes designed to promote quick movement within and across towers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/feed86f652bf34ec096d64f8c2adfff38e5843ce.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/cfbffce2ce3afc0f392f85be9d8f042adaca6337.jpg[/img]

One segment I am curious about is the protruding bit on the topmost floor of the blue building. I am not sure why it is there, maybe to block LoS when going from ceiling to the balcony below. Seeing this shape inspired me to experiment. Adding the green voxels and opening up a section in the wall allows players to jump outside, wallrun along the outermost edge while still being able to shoot toward the building, then return inside from another angle. The upper bit disallows simply jumping into the window from above, and the whole thing blocks LoS into and out of the room. I have yet to include such a structure in things I've made so far, so if it shows up in the future, know that this was my inspiration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/19a9333a87bed134796b13ab853157f72736c064.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/89ec44dd47c7f2bc89371d7078936c56b6d21b7d.jpg[/img]

While playing through the map there were times when firing the arm cannon at a building's walls did not lead to a new path, just a large dent in a thick structure. This was only easily confirmable in the level editor, as the rest of the map allowed smooth traversal with arm cannon destruction. A large section of the green and black tower is solid with certain sections hollowed out. Making a map with multiple buildings with interesting layouts that are unique in each given space is exceedingly difficult. It can be off-putting to not be able to go through something you thought you could go through, but it's easy to empathize with the creator if you are familiar with the process of making these spaces yourself. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/51faa10a7feadc13a903dd6dc48624c7c40af8f1.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/b74912b12a7daff63d54285831041ab2d4fab425.jpg[/img]

I could understand Towers being overlooked in the workshop if players stumble upon Towers 2 first, and may end up disregarding this level as a prototype for its successor. While similiar on the surface, both of Rick's original entries are worthy of exploration and completion and provide a fresh experience in both cases.

Making a good map is hard. Aesthetics, voxel types, lighting, layout and gemometry, enemy makeup and placement. All these things are examples of what needs to be taken into consideration when attempting to express an idea, concept, or emotion. I've been impressed with what I've seen other people make in the same level editor I use. I'm looking forward to seeing what other things gamers have to express, and I hope gamers look forward to the things I'd like to express in the future.

-bloody

notes.title: NEW IMPACT DRIVER ARM CANNON IS READY FOR USE!
notes.content:
[i][b]We wanted to take a moment to highlight some of the new features included with the most recent update ([url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1227690/view/3131686681089024348]Nov Patch 2[/url]), which was released yesterday. [/b][/i]

[h3][b]IMPACT DRIVER ARM CANNON[/b][/h3]
Taking the number of available arm cannons to three, joining the Plasma Grenade and Gravity Gun, the Impact Driver is a devastating melee weapon. It holds five charges and has two primary close-quarter functions: 1) destroying the environment and 2) sending enemies pinwheeling like ragdolls either into the distance or into the nearest solid surface. 

The Impact Driver in action:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/b5d04e1a76a30db4338b8c9c8037d35cfe120baa.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/fcf48b955b5f21b6aeadf65e61a20fffdd290450.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/ac542de3a19131474f695715b7a85bacb4170556.gif[/img]

[h3][b]FIREFIGHT PLAYLISTS[/b][/h3]
This feature simplifies the process of level selection in Firefight mode. Rather than having to return to the main Firefight menu screen each time you want to change the level you're playing on, you can now hit the 'Playlist' button, and add whichever levels you want to run through in your session. Then, after completing a level, you simply select the next level in your custom playlist if you want to keep going. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/b377057e0f7c0548d99e6a5051482cf0a445b46c.png[/img]

[h3][b]NEW EXPLOSION EFFECTS[/b][/h3]
Explosions are now much more explosive, with blasts creating more particles and debris. You can see before and after comparisons below, and the gifs above, particularly the last one, also show the new effect in action.

[b]OLD EXPLOSION EFFECTS[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/66a081af5f5ed9cec0a7c1192a5af2820b868fbe.gif[/img]

[b]NEW EXPLOSION EFFECTS[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/cd5a5fc4e75653e0c40a2b44b612ba71c20707b3.gif[/img]

[b]Note: The new explosion effect is currently disabled during RTX, but there will be a fix in a future update.[/b]

Thanks as always for your support and for playing Severed Steel. We hope you enjoy the new features, and don't forget there's even [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1227690/view/3052870530040434268][b]more additional content[/b][/url] still to come!

notes.title: COMMUNITY MAPS SPOTLIGHT
notes.content:
Time for another look at some level-editor created maps! You can find all these and plenty more to try in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1227690/workshop/]Steam Workshop[/url]. Please show your support for creators by leaving a positive rating on any map you enjoy playing. 

[h3][b]OMEGA TOWER (created by 'ZURA')[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/a86185a0c7f69dcdb682e45c711ed91e6625172e.jpg[/img]

Holy smokes, this is staggeringly good. Discovering and mastering the perfect line through this deftly designed, stunningly detailed and gorgeously lit cityscape, with its flowing wall-runs, and heart-stopping leaps between buildings, is a direct hit to the adrenal gland. Ace a run and it feels like a tightly choreographed action sequence worthy of any Hollywood blockbuster. Stupidly satisfying and highly recommended i.e. PLAY IT NOW.

[list]
[*] [b]GET IT: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2645749756]Subscribe to the map on Steam Workshop[/url][/b]
[/list]
[h3][b]SUBSITE ASTATINE (created by 'SN Empire')[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/00e16975082f261175a0881c21dd1ea117bc5eb7.jpg[/img]

Lavishly styled and devilishly intricate, this map has a real labyrinthine feel, despite being fairly compact. There are multiple routes and shortcuts tucked away that, once revealed and memorised, make this level a LOT of fun to navigate. The plasma arm cannon can be particularly well utilised here to create even more paths for you to choose from. Also, 'Subsite Astatine' is a cool name.

[list]
[*] [b]GET IT: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2603740012]Subscribe to the map on Steam Workshop[/url][/b]
[/list]
[h3][b]TOWERS 2 (created by 'Rick')[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/3792712d929ba24923a2670d524c395f870e1e89.jpg[/img]

A total contrast to Subsite Astatine in terms of scale, this is an expansive level, consisting of six detached, and differently colour-coded towers to work through as you do your best to reduce the intimidating enemy count. Prudently-placed fans and portals keeps traversal fast and fun, while some nice design touches ensure rooms are distinct and interesting. Big and ballsy ballistic action!

[list]
[*] [b]GET IT: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2637702663]Subscribe to the map on Steam Workshop[/url][/b]
[/list]
[h3][b]PARKOUR (created by 'Ouroborosso')[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/1c51e3f1bc5c547d7b95bbeddb60146f8231bce5.jpg[/img]

It may be a test or work-in-progress map, but we have to give it a shout-out as it's so cool to have a level that has no shooting or enemies. This level is 100% about the movement mechanics and getting from start to finish as quickly as possible, hitting the checkpoints along the way. We can't wait to see how this one evolves. Note: this map has objectives (a feature added to the level editor in the recent update), so once you've subscribed to it in Workshop, it's accessed via Mission Select in Campaign, rather than Firefight. 

[list]

If you fancy making your own map, but aren't sure how to get started, [b][url=http://discord.gg/cHsm52z]join the Severed Steel Discord[/url][/b] and head to the dedicated level editor channels for advice, guidance, and feedback.

notes.title: UPDATE – NOV PATCH 1. NEW GRAVITY GUN ARM CANNON AND MORE
notes.content:
The first of two updates we're releasing in November is now live. Patch notes and some extra detail below:
[list]
[*] New Game + mode (Random extra enemies and enemy respawns)
[*] Can use Firefight mutator unlocks in Campaign mode
[*] Gravity Gun arm cannon mode
[*] Lots of new small objects in world to throw around with the Gravity Gun
[*] 13 new Steam Achievements tied to Campaign
[*] Workshop levels can have Campaign objectives
[*] Overhauled 'Apartments' Campaign level
[*] Clearer enemy and objective outlines
[*] Lobber and RPG rounds now have tracer effect
[*] Level editor now supports user made props
[*] Reduced frequency of NPCs crouching in combat
[*] Update UE4 to 4.27.1
[*] Updated DLSS to latest
[*] Added hidden debug cam for content creators
[*] Fixed issue where kicking a door would sometimes hit door frame
[*] Fixed enemies hiding too well in lower admin campaign
[*] Fixed toilet shattering
[*] Fixed issue where NPCs would spawn without squad orders
[*] 'Estate' level can now also be damaged by explosives
[*] Option to disable camera roll
[*] Can no longer pickup empty weapons
[*] Added wffle to firefight unlocks
[/list]
[h3][b]NEW GAME+[/b][/h3]
Completing Campaign mode now unlocks New Game + on the Main Menu. As well as keeping you on your toes by remixing enemy placement, NG+ gives you the chance to play through Campaign with any unlocked Mutators switched on, and lets you choose which arm cannon you want to equip.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/8c199ea72c001f9c6f9c19df811fd247b8dafa57.png[/img]

[h3][b]NEW GRAVITY GUN ARM CANNON[/b][/h3]
Unlocked by completing 10 Firefight challenges, this new arm cannon lets you pick up, hold, and throw a variety of objects, enabling even more opportunities for gameplay experimentation. For example, you can grab and hold enemy shields to provide on-the-fly cover, and you can pluck rockets mid-air and reverse their trajectory for an explosive sucker punch, like so:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/e9b1361c6e4aee3e082eb89525043c932289cc7c.gif[/img]

[h3][b]NEW ACHIEVEMENTS[/b][/h3]
There are 13 new achievements to grab, which doubles the overall total to 26. The [url=https://steamcommunity.com/stats/1227690/achievements]full list can be found on the Achievements page[/url], but here are a couple of the new ones to give you a taster of what to expect: 

FIRE IN THE HOLE: Beat the 'Greens' campaign level with the 'Floor Is Lava' mutator
OFF THE HINGES: Beat the 'Corridor' campaign level while equipped with the 'Gravity Gun' arm cannon

[h3][b]AND THERE'S MORE TO COME[/b][/h3]
There's a second update coming later this month and, as [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1227690/view/3052870530040434268]previously mentioned[/url], there will also be updates next year, which will include new and extended Campaign levels. We'll have more info closer to the time. For now, have fun with New Game + and getting acquainted with the Gravity Gun!

Matt | Digerati

notes.title: NEW CONTENT FOR NOVEMBER AND BEYOND!

notes.title: FUTURE CONTENT UPDATES, COMMUNITY MAPS, SPEEDRUNNING
notes.content:
A lot to cram into this post, but before we get started, a massive thanks to everyone who has supported Severed Steel by buying and playing the game, leaving a review, streaming it, talking about it on social media, and anyone who has helped spread the word. We've been blown away by the response since we launched a week ago, so thank you.

Onto the post...

[h3][b]FUTURE CONTENT UPDATES[/b][/h3]
Severed Steel is not intended or designed to be a game that folks simply stop playing after a single completion of the campaign and, based on how much time we saw people putting into the pre-launch demos, we didn't think they would. However, we want as many players as possible to have a positive feeling about the game, so we want to do what we can to address complaints of it being too short. 

And the best way to do that is obviously with... MORE CONTENT!

We're happy to say more content is on the way, specifically a Campaign+ mode that allows mutators unlocked in Firefight to be enabled in Campaign. Also, the team is working on new levels for both Campaign and Firefight. However, we politely request your patience while Matt Larrabee, the developer behind the game, takes a break. Game dev and game launches can be an exhausting, brain-frazzling experience. Matt has worked tirelessly getting Severed Steel to this point, and he needs some chill time.

In addition to the new content already being worked on, we'd love to know what new features you'd most like to see added to the game. [b]So, click the following link and use the form to tell us what new/extra stuff you want in Severed Steel: [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1fJt7WChG5bvKqcMhqpNihtntr0htGuSarjjhj99Ieg0/edit]https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1fJt7WChG5bvKqcMhqpNihtntr0htGuSarjjhj99Ieg0/edit[/url][/b]

[h3][b]COMMUNITY MAPS[/b][/h3]
There are already some amazing maps created using the level editor for Firefight mode available to download from Steam Workshop, so we thought it would be cool to highlight a few of the ones we've been enjoying so far.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/a21cd0a6c84202e3be06428a172b7b1bb1328f96.jpg[/img]

A very cool approximation of the classic Counter-Strike desert-based map. It mixes open areas with narrow connection points, and CS players will recognise the starting area as the terrorist spawn location from the original. Don't forget you can use the rooftops, and watch out for flying enemies, which can be hard to spot/target against the bright sky.

This map is all about dramatic, action-movie flow and feel, and it's a thrill to play. Plenty of glass to smash through, buildings to leap between, small gaps to show off your stunt and movement skills, and a breathtaking rooftop slide. Oh, and it looks stylish as hell thanks to its neon-lit night setting. We've had a lot of fun here, perfecting our run and shaving seconds off our time. 
[list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/6ecf4fdde7a2e240d61a826e1039f96ac7c02157.jpg[/img]

Holy hell, this is HARD! There are 23 enemies surrounding you from the get-go, including two flamethrower dudes who take great joy in burning up the place, making it even more tricky as the house fills with smoke and flames. Even attempting this map on the easiest 'Cold Steel' difficulty is a serious challenge, but it's a cool scenario we have masochistically enjoyed playing.

notes.title: SEVERED STEEL INCOMING! HERE'S WHAT TO EXPECT...
notes.content:
With release day nearly upon us – Severed Steel arrives tomorrow (Friday, 17 September)!!! – we wanted to provide an overview of what to expect from the game on launch day. 

[b]Price:[/b] $24.99
[b]Digital Deluxe Edition price (includes game + OST)[/b]: $33.23
[b]Launch discount:[/b] 10% off for the first week
[b]Launch time:[/b] 10am PT/ 7pm CEST (make sure it's on your wishlist and you'll receive a notification when it's available) 

There will also be a Digital Artbook that anyone who owns the game will be able to download for free.

[h2][b]CAMPAIGN[/b][/h2]
This consists of six story chapters, and follows the journey of Steel, the game's leading lady and wall-running, gravity-defying, gun-toting badass. The action unfolds inside the sprawling HQ of nefarious mega-corporation, EdenSys, across a range of locations. Here's a layout of the building and, specifically, the areas you'll be covering: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/05f2ba3307bc4db0dccb17b95a9cc74e6889dd4b.jpg[/img]

Following an accident which leaves her with one arm, the campaign starts with Steel waking in a trash compactor after quite literally being thrown away by EdenSys. From this point, it's a whirlwind of hyper-kinetic acrobatics and slick gunplay as Steel sets her sights on revenge and goes after EdenSys' CEO. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/8fb60d8f451a568b7b5058c0d9b32f8631778828.jpg[/img]

In terms of campaign length, it will obviously vary from player to player, but an average for most folks will be around 2-4 hours to complete. There are reasons to replay, namely improving your level times and testing your skills on a harder difficulty setting, so there is more to juice from the campaign than just a single playthrough.

[h2][b]FIREFIGHT[/b][/h2]
Here's where you really get to test your skills. Firefight is an arcade-style mode where you'll be chasing high scores and fast times, with a spot on the leaderboards up for grabs. There are 30 levels to complete and unlock, and each level has its own set of challenges, such as getting a set number of headshots, killing a certain number of enemies while wall-running etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/dc1993b45df7b6923fc572d02884757b0b005a3c.jpg[/img]

Which of the five difficulties you select to play on can affect your final score. For example, playing on the hardest setting, 'Molten Steel', which starts you with just one single, solitary health point, increases your score by 200%. 

You can also choose your starting weapon, which – if you manage to unlock them all – totals 22 different guns to play with, including a range of pistols, shotguns, rifles, and some spicy numbers guaranteed to reduce enemies to a splattery mess of gibs. You also have your arm cannon, which spits plasma grenades capable of blowing holes in, well, pretty much anything.

Of course, as the one-armed Steel is unable to reload, you're constantly switching weapons, so have to get used to adapting on the fly.

Another cool feature of Firefight are the game modifying 'Mutators'...

[h2][b]MUTATORS[/b][/h2]
As you progress through Firefight, you'll unlock Mutators, which modify the game in a variety of weird and wonderful ways. You can apply multiple Mutators at once, although it's worth noting that scores aren't recorded on the leaderboard when a Mutator is enabled.

Here's a janky gif showing the game with the Big Head, Paintball, and Explosive Ammo Mutators all switched on: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/78a450517f866bb2837a1c825eea5331c02a4ee7.gif[/img]

Full list of current Mutators:

[list]
[*] Big Heads [easy headshots!]
[*] Super Slide [no limit on how much you can slide]
[*] Limited Slow Mo [twice as much slow-mo, but slow-mo meter doesn't recharge]
[*] Warrior Monk [you can't shoot, you can only throw guns]
[*] Paintball [guns make paint splats]
[*] Superkick
[*] Melee Gibs Enemies [melee kills cause enemies to explode]
[*] One In The Chamber [guns you pick up only have one bullet]
[*] Scary Lighting [darkens the level]
[*] Low Gravity 
[*] Floor Is Lava [luck drains while standing or running on the floor]
[*] Like Water [can start wall-running from a dive. Can start start a kickslide from a dive]
[*] Steelcraft [makes level cubic]
[*] See Through Walls
[*] Triple Threat [triple enemy threat]
[*] Thrust Cannon [shooting the arm cannon propels Steel]
[*] Steelcrawler [Steel goes invisible while performing a stunt]
[*] Enemies Explode On Death
[*] Explosive Ammo
[*] Cloaked [all enemies replaced with ninja type]
[*] Bulletproof [Steel can't die from weapons]
[*] Unlimited Ammo
[/list]
[h2][b]ACCESSIBILITY[/b][/h2]
To make Severed Steel enjoyable for as many people as possible, there are a range of accessibility features for navigation, controls, audio, and visual options. You can find a detailed breakdown at [url=https://www.taminggaming.com/accessibility/Severed+Steel]Family Video Game Database[/url]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/03b1024013df5d76c51a651f834c2675e6f70723.jpg[/img]

When low-mobility gamer and streamer 'onehandmostly' (aka Kyle) tried the Severed Steel demo, he called it 'the most accessible FPS I have ever played'! You can [url=https://youtu.be/L3CSOAv4ut4]watch his video here[/url]. 

In addition to the accessibility options, there are also five different - and widely ranging - difficulty modes to choose from. From easiest to hardest, here's what's included:
[list]
[*] [b]Cold Steel: [/b]A more relaxed experience. The enemy count is lower and enemies always drop guns with full ammo. Health recharges over time and you have unlimited bullet time.
[*] [b]Tempered Steel: [/b]The Severed Steel experience, but a little gentler. Enemy accuracy and reaction times are reduced, and you get a little extra invulnerability after taking damage. Restore health and bullet time by defeating enemies.
[*] [b]Severed Steel:[/b] The definitive Severed Steel experience. You may die a lot, but that only makes victory that much sweeter! Generous use of stunts required to survive. Restore health and bullet time by defeating enemies.
[*] [b]Sharpened Steel:[/b] The Severed Steel experience, but enemies do twice as much damage.
[*] [b]Molten Steel: [/b]For those who do not fear death. The Severed Steel experience, but with only one health point.
[/list]
[h2][b]LEVEL EDITOR[/b][/h2]
If you fancy having a crack at making your own levels, the editor tool lets you do that! Levels can be shared with the community via Steam Workshop and played in Firefight mode. In addition to community created levels, there will also be cut content created by the dev. Here's how you'll be to download the additional user-created Firefight maps: 

To access Steam Workshop from within Severed Steel itself, navigate to Firefight and click the “download” icon under the “Level Select” heading.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/48b18a437007b689c4406be34ed18b93342ee98b.png[/img]

Clicking this icon will open up the Steam overlay and take you to the Level Workshop. From there, feel free to browse and subscribe to any and all available content.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/6be61046b345941658a1903572a695aaaaddcc08.png[/img]

After you’ve subscribed to the content of your choosing, levels should download (and update) automatically. Once they’ve downloaded, all subscribed levels should auto-populate in the “Workshop” tab in the Firefight level select!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37614741/01adce9686cabfe979860cc1d33e3e45819d8e56.png[/img]

Keep in mind the Level Editor is still in a beta state as of this writing - be sure to check back often, content will only get better with time!

[h2][b]YOU'RE READY FOR SEVERED STEEL![/b][/h2]

Aaaaaaand, that pretty much covers everything. As well as the actual game, we'll also be releasing a new trailer tomorrow to celebrate the launch, so keep your eye out for that. Big thanks to everyone who has supported Severed Steel so far. If you downloaded any of the demos, participated in the betas, or wishlisted the game – thank you. We can't wait for you to play Severed Steel!

Matt | Digerati
